source: TESTING.md §7.8 table, hand-checked closed form. The table is quoted in percent (mean 0.250000 %, stdev 1.099242 %, vol 17.449928 %, return 63.000000 %, excess 61.000000 %, maxDrawdown -1.250000 %, sharpe 3.495716); the values here are those divided by 100, because this module works in decimal fractions. Tolerances are §7.8's, likewise divided by 100 for the percent-quoted rows (1e-6 % -> 1e-8, 1e-12 % -> 1e-14, 1e-9 % -> 1e-11). The ten returns are dated as consecutive calendar days from 2026-01-01, which is what makes the fifth return (-1.25 %) fall on 2026-01-05 as §7.8 states; the drawdown is that single return, from the 2026-01-04 peak, recovered on 2026-01-06.

TESTING.md §7.8 companion assertion: the population (n) stdev on the same series is 1.042833 % = sqrt(10.875/10) = sqrt(1.0875) in percent-squared, and the engine returns it ONLY because conventions.ddof = 0 is passed explicitly. Same series and same 1e-6 % tolerance as stats.vol.sharpe.10, in decimal.

Closed form on the fixed TESTING.md §7.8 series against a fixed synthetic benchmark (§7.8: 'Sortino, information ratio and beta use the same series against a fixed benchmark series in stats.beta.10, with OLS beta asserted against the closed form cov/var within 1e-12'). beta = cov(a,b)/var(b) with n-1 = 9 degrees of freedom: cov = 9.22222222222e-05, var(b) = 7.18222222222e-05, beta = 1.284034653465; alpha = mean(a) - beta*mean(b) per day, annualised x252; correlation = cov/(sd_a*sd_b), rSquared = correlation^2 = the OLS r^2; OLS standard errors on n-2 = 8 residual degrees of freedom; tracking error = sample sd of (a - b) x sqrt(252); IR = mean(a-b)x252 / trackingErrorAnnualised; Sortino target = riskFree/252 with four shortfall days. Values recorded to 12 decimal places, tolerance 1e-9 absolute (double-precision only).
